method: Ran the documented P4 worker ownership pytest command from examples/p4-durable-support, then ran the standalone SQLite teaching model suite from the repository root. Read the implementation of fence(), renew(), claim(), and all assertions in test_worker_ownership.py; compared the lesson's checkpoint tuples with the exact SQLite unit test setup. Reviewed the linked PostgreSQL 18 SELECT locking and date/time documentation.
limitations: The P4 takeover test force-kills owner A before worker B claims; it does not simulate a live worker recovering after network isolation.
No test holds a fenced transaction past lease expiry; wording about row-lock serialization is based on inspected implementation and PostgreSQL locking semantics.
No cross-machine clock skew, long GC pause, remote side effect, provider call, or exactly-once effect was tested.
The SQLite model uses injected integer time and does not prove PostgreSQL multiprocess scheduling behavior.
